solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clever person, not one for healthy food?

indicators.note: not one means the letter standing for one is left out of the word for a clever person

parts.note: a brain is slang for a clever person
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a clever person is somebody who shuns wholesome eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes I (one) from BRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran, the husk of cereal grain, is sold as a fibre-rich health food.

clue.text: Salt gives food item value

parts.note: a tart is a pastry dish, an item of food
rate means value, as in to rate something highly

explanation.surface: A seasoning is said to give a dish its worth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartrate is a chemical salt of tartaric acid, as found in wine deposits.

clue.text: Affected man at party you previously upset

parts.note: a stag is a man attending a stag party, the groom's night out before a wedding

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the old word for you is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of you

explanation.surface: A guest at a party once knocked you over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the old pronoun over. A stag party is a British men-only celebration before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagey behaviour is theatrical and exaggerated, which is what affected manners are.

clue.text: Becoming rude could make a son cringe

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be formed into something else by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Turning vulgar might cause a son embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges A SON CRINGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means rude or vulgar, so coarsening is becoming more so.

clue.text: Excel almost certainly with success in exam

indicators.note: almost means the word for certainly loses its final letter

parts.note: sure is an informal word for certainly
a pass is a successful result in an examination

explanation.surface: Doing brilliantly is all but guaranteed if you get through your test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SURE to SUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo or go beyond others, which is to surpass them.

clue.text: Music ultimately reaches heart

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word reaches, its final letter

parts.note: the core of something is its heart or centre

explanation.surface: A piece of music finally touches the listener's emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written form of a piece of music, so it can stand for music itself.

clue.text: PM could bring out reporters' bile

indicators.note: could bring out suggests the letters of the phrase can be drawn out and reshaped into a new name

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister might provoke the journalists' spleen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could bring out' rearranges REPORTERS BILE. Sir Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister in the 1830s and 1840s, founder of the Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Robert Peel served twice as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, so he is a PM.

clue.text: Jog along with husband in old-fashioned marriage pledge

parts.note: to trot is to jog along at a steady pace

explanation.surface: Someone runs gently beside a spouse while recalling an antique vow.
explanation.definitionFit: Troth is an archaic word for a pledge of faithfulness, as in plighting one's troth at a wedding.

clue.text: Long-term prisoner, Scotsman in coarse fabric

parts.note: Rudolf Hess, Hitler's deputy, was held in Spandau prison for over forty years
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A convict serving a long sentence and a Scot are dressed in rough cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is a rough woven cloth made from jute or hemp, used for sacking.

clue.text: Boy needs practice session to produce poetry

parts.note: a son is a boy child
in cricket, a net is a practice session in the netted practice area

explanation.surface: A lad needs rehearsal time to write verse.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, batters practise 'in the nets', so a net is a practice session.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line poem, a specific form of poetry.

clue.text: Extreme strictness is grim or nasty

indicators.note: nasty suggests something mangled or messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Severe rigidity is described as bleak or unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges IS GRIM OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigorism is a doctrine or practice of extreme strictness, especially in moral matters.

clue.text: Become embarrassed about a politician being insulting

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the phrase for blushing is read backwards

parts.note: to go red is to blush, becoming embarrassed
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone blushes over an MP who has been rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns GO RED into DEROG. TORY is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory remarks belittle someone, which is to say they are insulting.

clue.text: Mention top criminal having total control

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone names the gang boss who rules everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges MENTION TOP; 'top criminal' looks like a crime boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnipotent means all-powerful, wielding complete control over everything.

clue.text: Wicked demon has head chopped off

indicators.note: has head chopped off means the first letter of the word for a demon is removed

parts.note: a devil is a demon

explanation.surface: A fiend has been beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has head chopped off' removes the D from DEVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is an adjective meaning morally bad, a close synonym of wicked.

clue.text: Ancient doer of wrong in alliance

indicators.note: wrong means set awry or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old wrongdoer is part of a league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ANCIENT DOER OF; 'doer of wrong' looks like a phrase for a sinner, but 'wrong' is the anagram signal. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A confederation is a union of states or groups joined together, an alliance.

clue.text: Ford's place for getting wet?

parts.note: a ford is a shallow river crossing where one gets wet, but read Ford as the car maker and the place is where a vehicle is sprayed and scrubbed

explanation.definitionFit: A car wash is a facility where vehicles, such as a Ford, are washed with water.

clue.text: One tending certain insects — a very good skill is needed in that

parts.note: pi is crossword slang for pious, very good

indicators.note: needed in says the small word is placed within the word for skill

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beekeeper needs fine technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed in' puts IS inside ART to give ARIST. PI, short for pious, is a crossword convention for very good.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiarist is a beekeeper, someone who looks after bees.

clue.text: Little skip for which rubbish would be a bit too much

indicators.text: would be a bit too much
indicators.note: the word for rubbish has one letter more than wanted, so a single letter is dropped

parts.note: tripe is slang for rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: A short hop where a load of nonsense would be overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIPE is TRIP plus one extra letter, so dropping E gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a small skip or stumble on the feet, as well as a short journey.

clue.text: Latvian once in power acting without restraint

parts.note: Lett is an old name for a Latvian
taken as written
grip means power or control, as in a firm grip on the country

explanation.surface: A former Baltic citizen wields authority unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: To let it rip is an idiom for acting freely and with full force, without holding back.

clue.text: Fat monarch gets food supply

parts.note: lard is pig fat
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: A plump king receives provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the standard crossword abbreviation for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool pantry where a household's stock of food is kept.

clue.text: Fluid of the gods seen in rich ornamentation

indicators.note: seen in says the letters can be spotted running within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Divine liquid appears amid lavish decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, ichor is the ethereal fluid that flows in the veins of the gods in place of blood.

clue.text: Thus go round when you hear wine mentioned

indicators.note: when you hear, with mentioned later, says the phrase is spoken and the matching sound is taken

parts.note: so means thus and turn means go round

explanation.surface: Someone spins about whenever a vintage is named.
explanation.walkthrough: SO TURN said out loud matches the wine's name; 'mentioned' reinforces the spoken signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne is a sweet white dessert wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Hooligans rush and go wild

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Thugs charge forward and run riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges RUSH and GO; 'and' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughs is an old-fashioned word for violent, rowdy people, meaning hooligans.

clue.text: Strange objects visible to all, loud and huge

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all
F is forte, the musical direction for loud
OS stands for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Weird craft are seen by everyone, noisy and enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: UFOs are unidentified flying objects, which the clue loosely calls strange objects.

clue.text: Object first off to Ecstasy and joint

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter of the word for object is removed

parts.note: a thing is an object
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A complaint is raised, first to a drug and then to a dodgy cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' drops T from THING; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is a movable joint on which a door or lid swings.

clue.text: Girl gets round with little hesitation, rancher on horseback?

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl
O is round in shape
er is the sound of a brief hesitation

explanation.surface: A young woman turns, with a slight pause, toward a cowboy riding by.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a rancher on horseback may throw a rope loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A lassoer throws a lariat to catch cattle, typically a cowboy or rancher riding a horse.
